results.note: bare `deep` ignores the recipe that came before it and runs on the configured backend (`claude,deep` becomes two backends)
the recipe inserted before a lone deep step runs on the configured backend, not the deep step's (`deep:codex` no longer one backend, two passes)
the one-recipe-per-plan guard checks the wrong kind: `--ai a,b` is accepted and builds two recipe steps
None-vs-truthiness: an empty-string config value is no longer normalised to prompt-only
boolean flip: the plan line prints for recipe-only plans and is silent for the deep plans it exists for
wrong index: AiOptions.backend is the last step's backend, so `claude,deep:codex` reports codex as the backend
deep-escaped falls through every branch: NOT KEPT, the reports and the escapes are never printed
None-vs-truthiness: an empty summary prints a blank indented line (only the parts that exist)
wrong field: the printed --variant hint carries the file stem instead of the answer number
a previously chosen answer wins over the answer the person actually put in `.merged`, so --accept asks with the wrong guarantees and `chosen` never moves
the deep step never reads the recipe's proposal; it always reads git's diff3 merge, conflict markers and all
a skipped deep step no longer leaves the item pending, so the recipe's copy block runs as if the deep step had answered
reordered steps: the record with the moved `chosen` is written before the question, so chosen moves on a no as well as a yes
and/or swap: a previously accepted record is not asked again when the answer differs, and a never-accepted one is only asked when it does
removed guard: the loss and invention checks become a tripwire for every item, so a recipe proposal or a hand edit that drops lines is no longer gated
comparison flip: the loss check gates and the marker check is reported only -- the opposite of the split
when the recipe had nothing to decide, the deep step is skipped with a 'resolve that first' reason instead of reading git's clean merge
boundary: a live path with exactly target+rel parts yields Path() (the cwd) as the territory root instead of None
the pre-plan default is dropped: options built without steps run no AI step at all
dropped normalisation: the same endpoint with and without a trailing slash yields two identities (two cache keys)
